newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco's cement sales to reach $287 mln in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Morocco's cement sales to reach $287 mln in 1997.

text.p: Morocco's cement sales is expected to reach 2.7 billion dirhams ($287 million) in 1997 from 2.5 billion dirhams in 1996, a Casablanca-based research group said on Thursday.

"Acording to our forecast, we expect the cement sector sales to reach 2.7 billion dirhams this year against 2.5 billion dirhams in 1996," Mouna Tkito, a market analyst at Casablanca Finance Intermediation told Reuters.

"Some are more optimistic on the oulook for the cement output anticipating 5.0 or even 6.0 percent growth a year between now (1996) and the year 2010, providing gross domestic growth firms up at around 6.0 percent a year," the group said in a report.

If the industry grows at between 3.0 and 5.0 percent, the Moroccan cement output will stand at 6.7 million tonnes at the end of 1997 before reaching about 10 million tonnes in 2005 and 12.5 million tonnes in 2010, the Casablanca Finance Intermediation (CFI) said.
"For 1997, we predict cement volume to grow by 4.0 percent and value by 3.0 percent, based on a price increase of 3.0 percent and a inflation rate at around 5.0 percent," the group said.
Morocco needs 140,000 housing units annually to respond to a shortage and increasing demand of a population growing by up to 600,000 people every year, the report said.
But Moroco can only build between 80,000 and 90,000 units by year because of lack of active mortgage market.
"The effect of the current lack of funds for housing is that 70 percent is spent on villas and luxury apartments, which account for only 30 percent of housing needs," the group said.
CFI said the housing financing system has to be improved in order to reduce gap between average family income and the average price of houses throught the North Africa country.
Estimates put Moroccan typical home of 105 square metre cost at roughly 240,000 dirhams ($25,530). Average annual family income is estimated at 15,000 dirhams ($1,595), the report said.
The Moroccan cement industry is strained by heavy transport cost and no cement plant could survive if it has to transport cement more than 200 km (125 miles) from its processing site.

"This means that the cost of transporting cement 100 km (62 miles) can absorb up to 10 percent of the selling price per tonne. In Morocco, the natural market for cement is limited to a radius of 200 km (125 miles) around each cement works," the research group said.
Morocco's cement import and export are marginal, it added.
Morocco has 10 cement firms, including La CIOR, Ciments du Maroc, Asmar, Lafarge Ciment .
